heroHeadline: Trump Sends New Nuclear Proposal; Iran Advisor Says 'Ready to Sign'; Lebanon-Israel Ceasefire Extended 45 Days; Israel Strikes Lebanon Despite Extension; Oil Stockpiles Near Record Lows — Day 78
heroSubtitle: Day 78 (May 16): President Trump dispatched a new nuclear proposal to Iran requiring enrichment halt, HEU transfer to a third country, and international monitoring — offering congressional approval and full sanctions relief in return. Iran's Supreme Leader advisor Ali Shamkhani responded that Tehran is 'ready to sign the nuclear deal in exchange for the quick removal of all financial sanctions,' but called Trump's desired control over Iran's program a 'fantasy' and named Netanyahu as the 'main obstacle' to a deal. The Lebanon-Israel ceasefire was formally extended by 45 days by the US State Department, with a new military-to-military security track launching May 29 and political negotiations scheduled June 2–3. Within hours of the extension announcement, Israel ordered evacuations in nine southern Lebanese towns; at least 9 people were killed in airstrikes including 6 at a civil defense center near Tyre (3 paramedics). Lebanon's Health Ministry death toll rose to 2,951+ since March 2. On the energy front, global oil stockpiles are approaching record lows — UBS forecasts depletion by end of May; JPMorgan projects critical levels by September; S&P 500 fell 1.1% from record highs on stockpile data. Day 77 recap: Araghchi at BRICS New Delhi accused UAE of 'active role' in the war; Indian cargo ship sank off Oman; 30+ vessels transited Hormuz under Iranian 'cooperative' framework; Iran's judiciary claimed right to seize US-connected tankers.
